From c5b6285aae050ff1c3ea824ca3d88ac4be1e69c8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 14:52:41 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: SOF: Don't allow pointer operations on unconfigured
 streams

When reporting the pointer for a compressed stream we report the current
I/O frame position by dividing the position by the number of channels
multiplied by the number of container bytes. These values default to 0 and
are only configured as part of setting the stream parameters so this allows
a divide by zero to be configured. Validate that they are non zero,
returning an error if not

Fixes: c1a731c71359 ("ASoC: SOF: compress: Add support for computing timestamps")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260326-asoc-compress-tstamp-params-v1-1-3dc735b3d599@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/sound/soc/sof/compress.c b/sound/soc/sof/compress.c
index f4c3e10e6344..93f2376585db 100644
--- a/sound/soc/sof/compress.c
+++ b/sound/soc/sof/compress.c
@@ -381,6 +381,9 @@ static int sof_compr_pointer(struct snd_soc_component *component,
 	if (!spcm)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
+	if (!sstream->channels || !sstream->sample_container_bytes)
+		return -EBUSY;
+
 	tstamp->sampling_rate = sstream->sampling_rate;
 	tstamp->copied_total = sstream->copied_total;
 	tstamp->pcm_io_frames = div_u64(spcm->stream[cstream->direction].posn.dai_posn,
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `sound/soc/sof/compress.c`**
- In the function `sof_compr_pointer()`, added a guard condition before the calculation of `pcm_io_frames`:
  ```c
  if (!sstream->channels || !sstream->sample_container_bytes)
      return -EBUSY;
  ```
  This ensures that both `channels` and `sample_container_bytes` are non-zero before proceeding. If either is zero, the function returns `-EBUSY` instead of dividing by zero in the subsequent `div_u64()` call.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The added validation is directly tied to the existing `div_u64()` calculation that uses `sstream->channels * sstream->sample_container_bytes` as the divisor. Without this check, an unconfigured stream (where these fields default to 0) would cause a division-by-zero error when `sof_compr_pointer()` is invoked. The modification prevents that crash by returning an error status early.
- This change does not alter any other logic or affect other functions; it is a targeted fix addressing the specific vulnerability in pointer reporting for compressed audio streams.

Here is the commit message:
ASoC: SOF: Don't allow pointer operations on unconfigured
 streams

When reporting the pointer for a compressed stream we report the current
I/O frame position by dividing the position by the number of channels
multiplied by the number of container bytes. These values default to 0 and
are only configured as part of setting the stream parameters so this allows
a divide by zero to be configured. Validate that they are non zero,
returning an error if not

Fixes: c1a731c71359 ("ASoC: SOF: compress: Add support for computing timestamps")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260326-asoc-compress-tstamp-params-v1-1-3dc735b3d599@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The `sof_compr_pointer` function performs a division using `sstream->channels * sstream->sample_container_bytes` as the divisor, but these values are not guaranteed to be non-zero before the stream parameters are set. When they default to 0, a divide-by-zero error occurs, causing a crash or undefined behavior.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int sof_compr_pointer(struct snd_soc_component *component,
 			     struct snd_compr_stream *cstream,
 			     struct snd_compr_tstamp64 *tstamp)
 {
 	struct snd_sof_pcm *spcm;
 	struct snd_soc_pcm_runtime *rtd = cstream->private_data;
 	struct sof_compr_stream *sstream = cstream->runtime->private_data;
 
 	spcm = snd_sof_find_spcm_dai(component, rtd);
 	if (!spcm)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
+	if (!sstream->channels || !sstream->sample_container_bytes)
+		return -EBUSY;
+
 	tstamp->sampling_rate = sstream->sampling_rate;
 	tstamp->copied_total = sstream->copied_total;
 	tstamp->pcm_io_frames = div_u64(spcm->stream[cstream->direction].posn.dai_posn,
 					sstream->channels * sstream->sample_container_bytes);
 
 	return 0;
 }
